competency_fulfillment.rationale: Estimation means arriving at a reasonable figure for a quantity you have not measured. Every sample here hands the learner an exact measurement and then asks About how many meters is that under a rounding instruction. That is a rounding exercise wearing an estimation label; the competency's verb is never performed, because there is nothing left to estimate once the true value is printed in the stem.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The three quantity types named do appear, centimetre lengths, metre lengths and metre distances. What is absent is any other route into estimation: no choosing the most reasonable of several candidate measures, no benchmark comparison against a known referent, no estimate-then-check pairing. One sub-skill stands in for the whole competency.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Rounding to the nearest 5 m is not a standard early-primary rounding benchmark and does not follow from this measurement competency; deciding that 18 sits nearer 20 than 15 requires halving an interval that is not a power of ten. That is an extra procedural demand layered on top of a Grade 2 Quarter 2 measurement objective.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All thirteen seeds instantiate a single sentence frame: an object or span measures some value, followed by a request to round it. Only the noun, the number and the rounding benchmark move. There is no word-problem setting, no visual referent, no alternate orientation, and no item where the answer is a judgment rather than a rounded numeral.

competency_alignment.rationale: The difficulty dial being turned is rounding granularity, nearest 5 against nearest 10, plus the size of the starting value. Neither dimension belongs to estimating length or distance; a learner who improves across this progression has become better at rounding, not better at judging how long something is.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The underlying quantities are sensible for the objects named, with book and ruler lengths in the low twenties of centimetres and school-ground distances between roughly 14 and 35 metres. No value sits outside what a Grade 2 learner could plausibly encounter or handle.
